rationale: An implementation's declared corpus may only grow. Without this, a regression can be hidden by silently dropping the failing case: 8/8 stays green while coverage quietly falls to 7. Reducing declared support is therefore a deliberate, reviewable act — it requires editing this file, which appears as a visible diff and demands a justification.
enforcement: conformance/verify.mjs fails when an implementation declares fewer cases than its baseline, naming every dropped case.
subsystemCompletionMeaning: A subsystem is listed complete when every corpus case exercising it is declared AND the mutation battery (conformance/mutants.mjs) shows the corpus kills each declared semantic mutation of that subsystem's rules, with the predicted violation observable in the mutant's own output. Coverage counted only as a fraction is not evidence: before the boundary corpus landed, edge derivation reproduced its declared hash while eight of ten semantic mutations survived undetected.
mutationAdequacy: Listing a subsystem here does NOT assert mutation adequacy. conformance/REPORT.json reports the two claims separately, per subsystem: fixtureStatus and mutationStatus. A subsystem with no declared mutants is reported 'not-assessed' and carries no mutant counts, because 'we looked and found no survivors' and 'we never looked' are different epistemic states. Only 'edge-derivation' is currently mutation-qualified; the other nine are pinned by assumption.
authorizedReductionRequires: an explicit edit to this file recording the dropped cases and why
a justification naming the regression or protocol change
a ledger entry when the reduction accompanies a release
